articles.summary: As customers celebrate National Clean Energy Month and prepare for cooler weather, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) is encouraging customers to take simple steps to reduce energy waste and lower bills. One often-overlooked source of energy comes from "vampire appliances" and electronics that continue drawing power even when turned off, also known as phantom or standby power. Unplugging idle devices and using free tools can help customers identify and reduce this hidden waste. Up to 10% of a home's electricity bill may come from devices that continue drawing power even when turned off, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). Idle energy loads also account for about 1% of global carbon emissions, according to LBNL. The average U.S. household can spend $100 each year powering electronics that are not being used, according to the Department of Energy (DOE). That number can rise depending on how many always-on devices you have in your home and where you live.
articles.title: Preventing Phantom Power from Taking a Bite out of Your Budget This National Clean Energy Month

articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) continues to monitor a potential dry offshore wind event forecasted to start Wednesday evening, October 14, lasting through Saturday morning, October 17. As weather conditions continued to evolve, the event scope has been updated, adding approximately 25,000 customers and removing approximately 7,300 customers. articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) has filed a proposed 10-Year Electrical Undergrounding Plan (EUP) with the California Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety (Energy Safety), outlining a long-term, risk-based strategy to improve safety and reliability in high wildfire-risk areas across Northern and Central California that delivers long-term benefits valued at $117 billion. The proposed plan would place approximately 5,000 miles of electric distribution lines underground from 2028 to 2037 in locations where undergrounding is forecasted to provide the greatest reduction in wildfire risk. In these areas, undergrounding powerlines can reduce ignition risk by nearly 98% and improve reliability with 90% fewer outages. PGE estimates that completing 5,000 miles of undergrounding will also save customers approximately $6 billion in vegetation management, operations and maintenance costs over the life of these assets. articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) is monitoring a potential dry offshore wind event forecasted to start Wednesday evening, October 14 through Saturday evening October 17. The strongest winds are expected in the Sierra, southern Central Coast and portions of the North and East Bay. Given this wind event and current dry conditions, including extremely dried vegetation, PGE sent one-day advance notifications Tuesday afternoon to customers in targeted areas where PGE may need to proactively turn power off for safety to reduce the risk of wildfire from energized powerlines. The potential Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) event, starting Wednesday evening and forecasted to last through Saturday afternoon, could affect approximately 70,000 customers across twenty-nine counties. articles.summary: Eligible small business customers across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PGE) service area will automatically receive a $36.18 California Climate Credit on their October energy bill. No action is required to receive the credit. The twice-a-year electric credit was first delivered to eligible small business customers in April, for an annual total of $72.36 in credits distributed in 2026. The California Climate Credit is funded by the state's Cap-and-Invest Program (formerly known as Cap-and-Trade), which requires companies to pay for climate pollution. articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) has become the first energy utility in the world to earn accreditation from the Emergency Management Accreditation Program (EMAP), an independent, internationally recognized third-party organization. The accreditation validates PGE's emergency management capabilities across preparedness, response and recovery—essential responsibilities for a utility serving more than 16 million customers in Northern and Central California. According to EMAP , in order to earn accreditation, organizations must demonstrate compliance with all 73 emergency management standards . PGE met those standards with zero nonconformances identified during its assessment, demonstrating that its emergency policies, plans and practices meet EMAP's requirements.
